definition: Philosophy of science is a way of examining how a scientific idea is formed, whether its assumptions are plausible, and how it comes to be accepted as empirically supported. In this context, it is used to critically assess the scientific integrity of a diagnostic concept before and alongside research evidence.

reasons: The packet does not provide a general definition of “philosophy of science” as “a way of examining how a scientific idea is formed…whether its assumptions are plausible, and how it comes to be accepted as empirically supported.” It only states that the author “use[s] a philosophy of science framework to track the initial thinking, the plausibility, and the acceptance of ADHD.”

The packet supports the idea of using a “philosophy of science framework” to assess “scientific integrity” of ADHD, but it does not explicitly justify the broader framing in the definition (e.g., “before and alongside research evidence” or “empirically supported”) as characteristics of the term itself.

The phrase “how it comes to be accepted as empirically supported” is not supported by the packet; the source says ADHD was accepted in DSM-III through bias and compromise and concludes it is not empirically confirmed.

“Before and alongside research evidence” goes beyond the packet, which supports examining initial thinking and plausibility prior to empirical investigation, but does not state that the framework is used alongside research evidence in general.
